SEVERO C. MADRONA, JR. 26 AUG 2014 City Legal Officer Office of the City Legal Officer Pasay City, Metro Manila Dear Atty. Madrona, Jr.: This refers to your 02 May 2014 letter requesting this Department's legal opinion on whether or not hazard pay, subsistence and laundry allowance may be given to the employees of the following offices, to wit: (a) Office of the City Administrator; (b) Pasay Social Welfare and Development Office; (c) Pasay Public Cemetery and Crematorium; ('dj City Veterinarian Office; (e) City University of Pasay; and (f) Barangay Tanods; and whether or not City employees in the Social Welfare and Development Office, Public Cemetery and Crematorium, and Veterinarian Office are considered "health workers" as defined under Republic Act No. 7305 (RA 7305), otherwise known as the "Magna Carta for Public Health Workers. " The following are the discussions relative to your queries: Pursuant to Section 51 of the General Provisions of Republic Act No. 106331 (hereinafter, "FY 2014 GAA"), the grant of hazard duty pay (HDP) to officials and employees who are actually assigned to and performing their duties in strife-torn or embattled areas shall be subject to the rules and regulations prescribed under Budget Circular No. 2005-42 (BC 2005-4), dated 13 July 2005, and other pertinent rules and regulations issued by the DBM. BC 2005-4 applies to government personnel of local government units but excludes from its coverage those entitled to HDP or other similar allowances under existing laws such as public health workers (PHWs) and those who are not actually assigned to nor performing their duties and responsibilities in strife-torn or embattled areas, as may be determined and certified by the Secretary of National Defense, among others. Nonetheless, PH Ws are entitled to hazard pay pursuant to DBM-DOH Joint Circular No. 1, s. 2012, entitled: Rules and Regulation on the Grant of Compensation-Related Magna Carta Benefits to Public Health Workers (PHWs), provided they fall under the definition General Appropriations Act, FY 2014 2 Rules and Regulation on the Grant of Hazard Duty Pay

Section 67 of EO 292 was modified by Section 24 of RA 7305 which grants laundry allowance to PHWs in hospitals, sanitaria, health infirmaries, or other health-related establishments, to defray the cost for washing and pressing their personal protective clothing or uniforms required to be worn at all times while working, subject to DBM- DOH JC No. 1, s. 2012. Balangay Tanods Under Section 393 (a) of Republic Act No. 7160, barangay tanods are entitled to receive honoraria, allowances and other emoluments viz: "Section 393. Beiiefits of Barangay Officials. (a) Barangay officials, including barangay tanods and members of the lupong tagapamayapa, shall receive honoraria, allowances, and such other emoluments as may be authorized by luw or barangay, municipal or city ordinances in accordance zpitll the provisions of this Code xxx. ' The limit/ceiling for the grant of the same should not exceed_the minimum salary rate tor SG-I of the salary schedule being implemented by the city/municipality where the barangay belongs, provided further that such compensation shall not exceed those of the lowest paid barangay officials pursuant to Local Budget Circular No. 63, dated 22 October 1996, and Item 9.3.4.12.5 of the Manual on Position Compensation Classification- Chapter Notably, only barangay personnel who are paid salaries and whose positions are classified in accordance with Republic Act No. 6758 and issued appointments in accordance with the Civil Service law, rules and regulations pertaining thereto, may be entitled to the following benefits: personnel economic relief allowance (PERA); additional compensation; year-end bonus and cash gift; productivity incentive benefits; and other benefits accruing to regular employees.7 Hence, barangay tanods are not entitled to receive other forms of remunerations except honoraria, allowances, and other types of emoluments authorized by law or ordinance. 6 Source: http://www.dbm.gov.ph/wp•content/uploads/2012/03/Manual-on-PCC-Chapter-9.pdf(25 June 2014)

Interpretation or "HeaIth Workets" Anent the query on whether Pgsay City employees in the Social Welfare and Development Office, Public Cemetery and Crematorium, and Veterinarian Office are considered "health workers," it should be noted that the interpretation of the provisions of R.A. No. 7305 properly belongs to the Department of Health (DOH) as the agency primarily mandated to implement the same. It should be emphasized that the foregoing discussions are not intended iO supplant audit disallowances by the COA, if any, and any contrary opinion rendered by said agency and the DBM as the agencies primarily mandated to ensure the efficient and effective management and utilization of government funds. Moreover, payment of allowances, incentives and other benefits of government ofhciåts and employees (NGAs, LGUs, and GOCCs and their Subsidiaries) shall be governed by COA Circular No. 2013-003, as amended by COA Circular No. 2013-003A, and other issuances relative to thc grant of thc same. We hope to have enlightened you on the foregoing. Very truly yours, AUSTERE A. PANADERO Undersecretary for Local Government DILGOUSIG
